speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand the nature of these skin lesions, could you please describe what they look like and where on the body they are located?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: The description of painless, nonpruritic papules on the abdomen, especially with recent exposure to similar lesions in a daycare setting, is highly suggestive of molluscum contagiosum. Do the lesions have a central dimple or umbilication, and have they spread to other areas like the face or extremities?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of skin-colored, pearly papules with central umbilication is pathognomonic for molluscum contagiosum. DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum contagiosum
